messages:
Nora: Heads-up: sketching a follow-up to the billing pipeline RFC. Focus is on provisional ledger semantics and safe fanout. Posting rough notes so we can surface edge cases before the formal doc.

Li: Nice. Quick ask: why provisional ledger rather than single final write?

Nora: Two reasons: 1) UX/latency 3 quota checks and billing UI need near-immediate visibility, 2) audit/verifiability needs richer payloads that are heavier to produce and store. Provisional lets us show immediate effects while audit finalizes balances.

Omar: Implementation idea: single ingest point writes a tiny envelope to the ingress topic. Server-side fanout copies to a hot 'provisional' topic (compact, low-retention) and to an immutable 'audit' topic (cold, long-retention).

Priya: Important: provisional entries must be revocable and carry an idempotency/finality key. I'd prefer a canonical field: `claim_id` (uuid) + `schema_ver`. Reconciler uses `claim_id` to reconcile.

Nora: Agreed. Provisional record example (minimal):
```
{ claim_id, tenant_id, token_delta, ts, provisional_ttl_secs }
```
And audit record is full payload with provenance, model, prompt hashes, bucketed token breakdowns, raw token counts, request headers, etc.

Li: How do we avoid double-applying if reconciler emits a compensating event? We need a clear event-set for ledger transitions: PROVISIONED -> FINALIZED or PROVISIONED -> COMPENSATED.

Omar: We can model ledger as CRDT-like sequence of operations but simpler: treat ledger as append-only events plus a derived materialized view that consumes events in order with idempotency by `claim_id`. Compensations are just negative events with a ref to original claim.

Priya: Operationally, reconciler must be able to produce three outputs: 1) final-positive (no change), 2) final-no-op (audit matches provisional), 3) compensating-event (audit differs). Consumers of provisional should accept compensations; Console should surface provisional vs final for customers.

Nora: Retention policy: provisional topic short TTL (24-48h). Audit topic long TTL (90 days default, configurable per-tenant). For private deployments, TTLs will be customer-configured.

Li: What about backfills? If we replay audit for historical fixes, reconciler needs to be idempotent across replays. Suggest including `ingest_version` and `source_batch_id` for any backfilled events so reconciler can dedupe.

Priya: Also add an event fingerprint (sha256 of normalized payload) to make fuzzy equality checks faster for aggregated comparisons. Fingerprint stored in both lanes.

Omar: On scale: per-claim reconciliation provides strongest guarantees but could be expensive at 100k claims/sec. Proposal: default per-claim for first 30 days after rollout, then add batch reconciliation where claims are bucketed into minute-level groups and reconciler operates on buckets + per-claim exceptions.

Nora: Good call. We should also support tenant-tiered policies: startups get 24h finalization, enterprise can request SLA 1h or longer windows depending on their batch workflows. Expose policy via tenant config.

Li: How will quota enforcement interact with provisional state? If provisional can be revoked, we need a way to avoid user-visible quota oscillations in UIs and rate limits.

Priya: Rate limits should read from a `committed_balance` with a small provisional buffer allowance. Provisional consumption reduces available quota immediately but marked as provisional UI. If compensated, buffer is released and logs show compensating action.

Omar: UX suggestion: Console shows a two-line balance: "Available (finalized)" and "Reserved (provisional)" with an explain link. API endpoints can return `balance` and `provisional_reservations` fields.

Nora: Observability: we need metrics for fanout latency (ingest->provisional, ingest->audit), reconciliation lag, compensation rate (compensations / provisionals), and reconciliation error rate. Alert thresholds: compensation rate > 0.1% should trigger P1 investigation.

Li: Security: audit topic must be encrypted-at-rest and accessible only to auditing/reconciler roles. For private installs integrate with KMS; restrict read APIs.

Priya: A few failure modes: (1) provisional write succeeded, audit write failed -> reconciler sees missing audit after X window and marks as 'audit-missing' (alerts ops, keep provisional until retry/backfill), (2) duplicate provisional write -> dedupe by claim_id, (3) mismatched counts due to model tokenizer changes -> reconciler should use fingerprint and tokenization-version in audit payload to detect.

Omar: For (1) we need automated backfill pipeline and a 'pending-audit' queue with TTLbackoff. For (3) include `tokenizer_version` in audit_event.

Nora: On APIs: add a lightweight query `GET /v1/ledger/claims?claim_id=...` which returns provisional+final status and links to audit_event. Also admin API to force-reconcile or mark as accepted for special customers. Keep these admin actions logged.

Li: Thoughts on schema evolution: keep provisional minimal and stable. Audit schema uses semantic versioning and we attach `schema_ver` and `schema_date`. Reconciler will validate required minimal fields and ignore extras.

Priya: Testing plan: end-to-end canary with synthetic load, inject mismatches to validate compensating flows, run chaos tests (audit topic delay, reconciler downtime) and ensure no double-charges.

ingest-bot: Fanout smoke: provisional topic 0.2ms median, audit append 12ms median. Canary replay test completed with 5000 events.

Nora: Next steps: I'll formalize this into RFC draft. Priya will write dedupe/reconciler design sketch. Omar will propose fanout topology and monitoring signals. Li will enumerate API and UI surface changes. Sync Fri 9:30am?

Omar: Works for me.

Priya: +1

Li: +1

Nora: Thanks all. I'll drop the RFC link in here when ready.
